name: Cleft Lip and Palate-Craniofacial Dysmorphism-Congenital Heart Defect-Hearing Loss Syndrome
aliases: Cleft Lip/Palate with Craniofacial Anomalies and Cardiac Defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for CLP-CHD-HL Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral or bilateral cleft lip and/or cleft palate
Distinctive craniofacial anomalies including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Documented congenital heart defect such as ventricular septal defect or atrial septal defect
Sensorineural or conductive hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cleft lip and/or palate, craniofacial dysmorphism, congenital heart defect, and hearing loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral cleft lip and/or cleft palate
searchTerms: split or gap in upper lip and/or roof of mouth
cleft lip and/or palate on one or both sides
opening in lip or palate present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distinctive craniofacial dysmorphism including hypertelorism and micrognathia
pathognomonic.notes: Facial features are characteristic and aid diagnosis
searchTerms: unusual facial features including wide-set eyes and small jaw
distinct facial appearance with large eye spacing and small chin
facial differences with hypertelorism and micrognathia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital heart defects such as ventricular septal defect
searchTerms: birth defects of heart like septal holes
hearing loss from nerve or ear problems
difficulty hearing due to inner or middle ear issues

common.notes: Small lower jaw affecting feeding and airway
Due to cleft palate and craniofacial anomalies

occasional.notes: Mild delays reported in some cases
Related to cleft palate and hearing loss
Due to feeding challenges and cardiac defects

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to cardiac defect
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from heart defect
pulmonary hypertension caused by heart problem
lung blood vessel pressure increased due to cardiac defect

rare.notes: Reported rarely, possibly secondary to hypoxia

laboratory: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural or conductive hearing loss
imaging: Craniofacial CT or MRI showing dysmorphic features and cleft palate
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic facial features and cleft anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Typically autosomal dominant with IRF6 gene mutation
Distinctive facial features different from CLP-CHD-HL syndrome
Confirmed by FISH or microarray testing

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defect causing cyanosis or heart failure
Profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss impacting development
Airway obstruction due to micrognathia and cleft palate
references: Orphanet: Cleft lip and palate-craniofacial dysmorphism-congenital heart defect-hearing loss syndrome, ORPHA:508476
